title: Answer the 0500 with the receiver's verdict

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended: `src/main/java/com/example/practice/DayTotals.java` already counts the day correctly. Now the same class builds the `0500` and plays the receiving side. Your test lab uses it as a stand-in host: it gets the switch's `0500`, counts the same day from its own copy of the traffic, and answers.

`request` is written, except for the net settlement amount, DE 97. Finish `de97` and `answer`. The receiver's answer is only useful if it says `2` whenever the two ends counted the day differently, and the `0500` it received is evidence of what the switch said, so it keeps it as it came. About ten lines in total.
The tests build totals directly; they include a day of more refunds than sales.

cases.says: the 0500 carries the net as C and 16 digits and packs with iso87ascii
an 0500 whose totals equal the receiver's is answered 0510 with DE 39 00 and DE 66 1
an 0500 with a purchase the receiver never counted is answered out of balance
when refunds exceed sales, DE 97 is D followed by the net's absolute value
two counts with the same net but different categories are out of balance
answering builds a new message and leaves the received 0500 unchanged

origin.section: 19.4. The Receiver Compares Every Total, Because Equal Nets Can Hide Different Counts

concepts: The receiver of an 0500 compares every totals field with its own count and answers 2 when any differs, even when the nets agree; DE 97 is a C or D sign and 16 digits.
